newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN, DUTCH PAPERS COOPERATE IN SCREEN INFO.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN, DUTCH PAPERS COOPERATE IN SCREEN INFO.

text.p: Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd (FET) and its Dutch counterpart Het Financieele Dagblad have made a deal to offer electronic stock market information together.
The papers said in a joint advertisement in their Wednesday editions they will offer screen-based electronic information via their unit "TfD" (Tijd Financieel Dagblad).
"We are signing a general framework agreement for cooperation, which will include real-time stock prices and downloading of historical price data," FET managing director Paul Huybrechts told Reuters.
Both papers will also exchange correspondents and cooperate in advertising.
FET was already active in electronic news and price dissemination via FIA, a cooperation between FET unit "Tijd Electronic Services" and Dutch Financiele Diensten Amsterdam (FDA).
The cooperation with FDA has been ended and FIA -- which has some 500 clients in Belgium -- will be renamed TfD.
"We have parted with FDA on amicable terms," Huybrechts said.

The Windows-based TfD screens offer stock prices from all leading world markets, Eurobond quotes and foreign exchange quotes. They carry news from the parent papers as well as a selection of news from other sources, such as national news agency Belga and several international news agencies.
Data communication is free, as TfD uses the cable tv network.
"TfD is just the first step in a long march," said Huybrechts. The paper's publisher Uitgeverij Tijd also offers Internet and CD-rom database services.
